newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian Leu closes little changed.
newsitem.headline: Romanian Leu closes little changed.

text.p: Romania's leu closed little unchanged on Wednesday at 7,050/70 to the dollar in a market unmoved by a central bank (BNR) announcement of higher foreign exchange reserves, traders said.
"News of central bank's forex reserves at up to $1.6 billion in May failed to impress the market," one trader said.
On Wednesday, BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said the BNR foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.55-1.6 billion from $1.45 billion at end-April and should hit over $2 billion in June.
He said the rise had been triggered by capital inflows, purchases of dollars from the local interbank market and by direct foreign investments and repatriation of export earnings.
"That level was expected as the central bank has bought daily from the market recently so we were not impressed," another trader said.
On the money market, short terms rates hovered around 85 percent, while the overnight rate was at 80 percent. Operators said they expected rates to drift down due to excess leu funds on the market.
They said the BNR had taken no steps yet to drain the excess. It is necesary to launch instruments to drain a flooded money market, one trader said.
"The central bank obviously has to implement open market operations as soon as possible or issue certificates of deposit to mop up liquidity," said an operator.
Earlier this week Romania's central bank announced it was considering issuing certificates of deposit to drain excess funds from the local money market, but it did not elaborate.
Leu-dollar rates at licensed money changing bureaux were unmoved at around 6,900/7,000.
